name: Dara Sok
headline: 62, former logistics director, night inventory supervisor, Vancouver
title: A Sunday Invitation to the Community
situation: On a Sunday after sending the remittance, Dara stops by Granville Market for ginger. The clerk, who knows them by name, mentions that a group of Cambodian elders gathers at the community hall every Sunday afternoon to play traditional music and share stories. He invites Dara to join, saying they are welcome to listen or even try the tro. Dara has never attended, preferring their usual walk home and bowl of porridge. The invitation carries no pressure, yet it offers a taste of home in a foreign city. Dara could accept and spend an hour with the group, or politely decline and keep to their familiar Sunday rhythm.

context.relationship_profiles:
With the clerk: cordial and transactional, built on weekly remittance visits; the clerk knows Dara's name and exact money but nothing of their life.
With daughter Mei: a warm but worried bond; Mei pushes Dara to socialize, but Dara gently deflects with their usual saying.
With the elder group: no prior contact; Dara has passed the hall often but never entered.
context.tendencies:
When invited to social gatherings in Vancouver, Dara politely declines and keeps to their routine walk.
At work, they let misgendering pass to avoid friction, nodding and continuing.
They maintain fixed schedules, like arriving an hour early at the port.
context.current_state:
After the remittance, Dara feels the familiar distance from Phnom Penh but also a quiet sense of duty fulfilled.
Physically tired from the night shift, they crave their warm porridge and the stillness of home.
Curiosity about the music is present but dulled by the weight of unfamiliar interaction.
context.immediate_memories:
The clerk's mention of the tro brings back their mother humming to similar instruments at family feasts.
Seeing the hall's open door recalls a childhood village meeting where Dara sat silent among elders.
The smell of ginger from the market reminds them of their mother's porridge and her stories.
context.reflective_memories:
In Phnom Penh, Dara learned to keep their inner life private, especially around identity.
They have long believed that routine and duty are what hold a family together, even far away.
Even in Cambodia, they never joined communal singing, preferring to watch from the edge.
